*Sits on a small stool by the doorway, sipping tea*

Well, what can I say. I'm 68 this year. I only really started farming on my own last year — before that I worked odd jobs in town, came back to the village when my legs got bad and my wife said enough is enough. So I'm an old man but a new farmer. My wife helps me. Just the two of us at home now, the children are working in Shijiazhuang and Beijing, they don't come back much.

I've got 10.1 mu. Last year my neighbor Old Wang next door, he's been farming forty years, he told me how to split it. I put about 4 mu in cotton on the western piece — that land is a bit drier, and around here a lot of people still grow cotton on that kind of ground. The other 6 mu I did wheat in winter, then maize after — that's what most everyone does in our village. Last year wasn't bad. Got us through. So this year I'll do the same. I don't know any better way and changing things makes me nervous.

**For the wheat** (about 6 mu): I'll plant in early October, same time as last year, same time as Old Wang. I save some seed from last year's harvest, but I also buy a bit because Old Wang said new seed is better — I don't really understand why but I trust him. Before I plow I put down one bag of compound fertilizer per mu, about 25 kg, that's the standard around here. Then in early spring when the wheat starts standing up tall, I'll spread some urea on top, maybe 10 kg per mu. If I see it looks yellow I'll add a little more, but urea is expensive so I try not to overdo it. I'll irrigate two times — once before winter to make sure it survives, once in spring when it's heading. Each time I irrigate the well costs me money for electricity, so I don't do extra.

**For the maize** (same 6 mu, planted right after wheat): As soon as the wheat is cut in early June, we have to move fast — Old Wang told me you can't wait, the season is short. I'll have someone with a machine come do the planting, I pay him, my back can't handle it anymore. I put fertilizer in with the seed, compound, about 20 kg per mu. Then when it's about knee-high I'll topdress urea, maybe 10 kg. I irrigate once or twice depending on the rain. Last year it rained a lot so I only watered once.

**For the cotton** (about 4 mu): This one I'm less sure about. Cotton is more work — you have to spray for bugs, you have to pick by hand, my wife helps but it's hard on her hands. I plant in late April. I bought hybrid cotton seed last year, that's what's sold at the shop, I just buy what they have. I put down compound fertilizer before planting, maybe 25 kg per mu, then add urea once when it starts flowering. I have to spray for bollworm — I don't really know which spray is best, I just buy what the shop owner says is good for cotton. Pick three or four times in autumn, takes a long time, just me and my wife. If my daughter visits she'll help one weekend.

I don't have much cash. Whatever I make from selling cotton and maize last fall, that's what I have to spend on inputs this year. So I'm careful. I'd rather underdo the fertilizer a little than spend money I don't have. If something goes wrong — drought, hail — I have nothing to fall back on except what the children send. So I keep things simple and the same as last year.
